## Hands-on 1 – The setup check {#hands-on-1-the-setup-check .smaller}

::: {.small}
**Task 1 – the setup check.** Get to the point where a line of R runs and the data are in front of you.

- **Workspace:** your IDE opens the workspace folder, and `source("R/check_setup.R")` prints an `[OK]` line for every check; the last one fits a number that you will meet again later, `r fmt_num(curve_ref$b, 3)` on the log scale
- **Everything ships in `data/`:** the unions rebuilt from the survey, and the file that Multi100 gave the analysts, which Task 3 needs. Nothing to download
- **Browser lab:** the page has finished loading, the setup cell runs, and it reports `r fmt_n(nrow(unions))` cohabitations and the same `r fmt_num(curve_ref$b, 3)`
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Take the time you need, **into the break** if necessary. Type a green circle in chat when you are through; type **STUCK** and I will come to you.
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
If your installation will not cooperate, do not fight it – open the browser lab and carry on. Every task of the day runs there, the reproduction of Task 3 included.
:::

::: notes
Your turn, and this first task is deliberately not intellectual. The job is to reach the point where a line of R runs and the data are in front of you. In the workspace, open the folder in your IDE and source the check script: it prints one OK line for each thing that the course needs, and the last check fits a model and prints a number that you will meet again later, minus nought point seven three. Everything that the day needs is already in the data folder, including the file that the analysts received, so there is nothing to download. In the browser lab, wait for the page, run the setup cell, and check the two numbers. Take the time you need, into the break if you have to. A green circle in chat when you are through, STUCK if you need me.
:::
